clips.title: The story
paras: Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar sends you after a stolen emerald in northern Teldrassil. The jewel was pried from his damaged heirloom dreamcatcher by Gnarlpine furbolgs north of Starbreeze Village, and now hangs from their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater.

Tallonkai Swiftroot felt relief when the dreamcatcher recovered from the corrupted wilds came back to him, then dismay at its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame. Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the influence of a furbolg leader named Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. In Ferocitas's clutches, the sacred gem was useless and perverse, so Tallonkai sent defenders to take it back.

The Gnarlpine furbolgs in Teldrassil's northern reaches were once peaceful neighbors. Corruption seeping into the World Tree drove them into frenzy and madness. Their mystics once practiced harmonious nature rites, but began drawing on distorted magical energies. Travelers can track down Ferocitas by cutting through the mystics guarding his woodland enclave. The jewel can then be returned to Tallonkai, so his dreamcatcher may be made whole and balance restored to the woods.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: The emerald... It is missing! My dreamcatcher has been damaged!

There is a band of Gnarlpine mystics located to the north of Starbreeze. I have heard reports that their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater has been wearing a necklace that glows green in the night. Now seeing my dreamcatcher, I am sure that he has stolen my emerald... He would never realize that its power is useless to him.
Find this missing jewel, friend. And, while you're there, clear out some of the corrupted mystics as well.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Ferocitas and the Gnarlpine mystics must return what is mine. Please retrieve the emerald so that I may repair my emerald dreamcatcher.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Now I can repair my dreamcatcher. Thank you, friend.
